Fecal microbiota transplantation in cancer immunotherapy: targeting the Gut-Tumor Axis.

This review critically integrates clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence on fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as an adjunct to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) cancer therapy. It examines donor selection, microbiome remodeling, and the gut-tumor axis, noting that clinical responses remain inconsistent and that microbiome changes do not reliably predict benefit. The authors highlight fragmented evidence and call for more rigorous integration to guide FMT use in immunotherapy.

Current research in microbial sciences 2026-12-01 Medium

Lung microbiota in COPD: a double-edged sword.

This review argues that the lung microbiota in COPD acts as a 'double-edged sword,' where effects on disease depend more on overall community structure and ecological balance than on individual beneficial or pathogenic taxa. It frames the respiratory microbiota as a dynamic low-biomass ecosystem shaped by immigration, elimination, local growth, and host-environment interactions, and uses COPD as a model of profound ecological disruption.

Multiomics Approach to Regionally Profile Zinc-Driven Host-Gut Microbiome Interactions in the Intestinal Tract.

This study uses a multiomics approach to map how zinc deficiency alters host-gut microbiome interactions across different regions of the intestinal tract. The authors profile regional (spatial) changes in host and microbial molecular features, revealing that zinc's effects on the host-microbiome interface vary by intestinal location. This regional perspective helps explain why zinc supplementation trials have produced inconsistent results.

The ecological impact of Ulva prolifera green tide outbreaks: microbial connectivity and metabolic divergence.

This study uses amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to examine how Ulva prolifera green tide blooms affect microbial community dynamics across continuous microhabitats. The authors find that phycospheric microbiota show increased alpha-diversity and more complex network topologies, and that these microorganisms originate from surrounding environments, indicating the bloom enhances microbial dispersal and connectivity. The work also reveals metabolic divergence among microhabitats, highlighting the ecological impact of green tides on coastal microbial ecosystems.

Complete coding sequence of a virus belonging to the Chaphamavirus genus identified in a pooled blood sample from Actitis macularius birds collected on the Brazilian Amazon coast.

Researchers sequenced the complete coding region of a novel chaphamavirus from a pooled blood sample of spotted sandpipers (Actitis macularius) on the Brazilian Amazon coast. The genome is substantially divergent from known chaphamaviruses, indicating a distinct genetic lineage that may warrant taxonomic revision of the genus. This adds a new geographic and host record for an under-sampled viral group.

Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads.

DADEC is a new hybrid error-correction pipeline for noisy long reads that combines stringent de Bruijn graph correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive de Bruijn graph recovery in a confidence-ordered framework. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, it achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmarks while preserving genuine biological variation and avoiding over-correction.

Sheep or cattle fecal contamination? Using long-read amplicon sequencing for fecal source attribution and apportionment.

This study tests whether long-read amplicon sequencing combined with FEAST source-tracking and mitochondrial/MST qPCR markers can distinguish sheep from cattle fecal contamination in freshwater. Using a spiked laboratory experiment with known inputs plus field samples, the authors evaluate how well these approaches attribute and apportion contamination between two closely related ruminant sources. Genome-resolved multi-omics characterizes bacterial, viral, and metabolic components associated with Parkinson's disease gut ecosystem variation.

This study used deep shotgun metagenomics and fecal metabolomics to characterize gut bacteria, viruses, and metabolites in Parkinson's disease patients versus matched spouse controls from a high-altitude cohort. The authors reconstructed 455 species-level bacterial genome bins and 2,957 viral operational taxonomic units, enabling genome-resolved analysis of how bacterial, viral, and metabolic components of the gut ecosystem vary with PD. The work provides a high-resolution resource linking gut microbiome and virome features to PD-associated metabolic context.

Urban avian viromes reveal viral diversity of potential public health relevance across China.

This study performed a large-scale viromic survey of urban birds across 22 Chinese cities, identifying over 52,000 viral operational taxonomic units and revealing extensive previously underexplored viral diversity. Viral richness varied markedly among cities, driven largely by bacteriophage diversity, while vertebrate-associated viruses showed a narrower range. The findings highlight urban avian viromes as a reservoir of viral diversity with potential public health relevance.

Aerobic and anaerobic cultivation shapes steroid-degrading wastewater consortia: Metagenomic insights into catabolic potential and antibiotic resistance genes.

This study enriched microbial consortia from dairy and municipal wastewater on the steroid hormones progesterone (P4) and 17β-estradiol (E2) under aerobic and anaerobic conditions, combining degradation kinetics with shotgun metagenomics. Aerobic consortia removed >99% of P4 within 9–12 hours and E2 within 24 hours, far outperforming anaerobic conditions. Metagenomic analysis linked these differences to catabolic gene potential and revealed antibiotic resistance genes carried by the steroid-degrading communities.

Broad-spectrum in situ genetic reprogramming of native microbiomes.

The authors developed SPARTA, a method that uses engineered broad-spectrum phage particles to deliver and integrate large synthetic DNA constructs directly into diverse microbial taxa within native communities. This provides a one-step strategy for reprogramming microbiome functions across varied ecosystems.

Melon fruit microbiomes resemble aerial-tissue communities in a Turpan oasis field.

This study profiled bacterial and fungal communities across rhizosphere soil, roots, stems, leaves, and fruits of four field-grown melon cultivars at two developmental stages in a Turpan oasis. The key finding is that melon fruit microbiomes more closely resemble aerial-tissue (stem/leaf) communities than root or soil communities, suggesting that fruit-associated microbes are primarily acquired from aboveground sources rather than vertically from the soil. This clarifies the position of fruit communities within the whole-plant microbiome of a field-grown crop.

Shotgun Metagenomics Versus 16S rDNA Sanger Sequencing for the Diagnosis of Blood Culture-Negative Endocarditis: A Draw?

This study directly compared shotgun metagenomics and 16S rDNA Sanger sequencing on identical DNA extracts from surgically removed heart valves in patients with blood culture-negative infective endocarditis. Both methods showed similar positivity rates for detecting pathogens, but metagenomics provided higher taxonomic resolution. The findings suggest that while both approaches are viable, metagenomics offers an advantage in identifying organisms to the species level.
